Here's a LinkedIn cut. **Hook archetype:** specific number + contrarian claim (the cost surprise wasn't where you'd expect). **Structure:** hook / proof / payoff / one ask.

---

## Hook (first 3 seconds)

**On-screen text:** "Our second café cost 40% more than the first."
**VO:** "Our second location cost 40% more than the first — and rent wasn't the reason."

*Visual: you, to camera, in the new space mid-fit-out. First line is the whole hook — it has to land before "see more" on LinkedIn.*

---

## Body (3-4 scenes with cues)

**Scene 1 — the assumption (0:03–0:18)**
VO: "We budgeted like rent was the big line. Bigger room, bigger lease, done."
On-screen: "What we planned for: RENT"
*Cue: cut to the signed lease / floor plan on a table.*

**Scene 2 — the real cost (0:18–0:40)**
VO: "The actual overrun was people. We hired a full team three weeks before opening so they could train together — not trickle them in like we did at site one. That overlap is wages with no revenue behind them yet."
On-screen: "What actually cost us: STAFFING"
*Cue: the team in the empty café doing a dry run — pulling shots, no customers.*

**Scene 3 — why it was worth it (0:40–0:55)**
VO: "Site one took four months to feel like it ran itself. Site two ran clean on day one — because we paid for the overlap up front instead of bleeding it in mistakes later."
On-screen: "Day-one service vs. four months of fixing it"
*Cue: busy, smooth service shot — the delta made visible.*

---

## CTA

**On-screen text:** "Front-load the staffing, not the panic."
**VO:** "If you're opening a second site, the number worth modelling isn't the rent — it's the paid overlap before you open. Curious whether other operators front-load it the same way, or if we overpaid for peace of mind."

*Cue: back to you, to camera, in the finished space during service. One ask — an opinion, which is what LinkedIn rewards and what won't get suppressed as a reaction prompt.*
